verdicts.correction: 2 x 8 x 1 x 512 x 2 = 16,384 B. Sliding per token of window: 2 x 40 x 8 x 256 x 2 = 327,680 B. Also confirmed for llama.cpp: src/models/gemma4.cpp:279-290 at b12418 sets Vcur = Kcur when wv is absent but then normalizes K with attn_k_norm weights and V with a weightless rms_norm, so K and V differ and V is cached separately: no halving in llama.cpp either (resolves a listed gap).

verdicts.claim: vLLM sliding-window reservation is (window-1 + max_num_batched_tokens 2048) = 3071 tokens = 0.937 GiB BF16, giving about 193,300 tokens max BF16 context (est_max_context_tokens 193000)
verdicts.correction: v0.33.0 sizes sliding groups with max_in_flight_tokens = max_concurrent_batches x max_num_batched_tokens (vllm/config/vllm.py:588-609). Async scheduling is on by default (vllm.py:1685-1719), giving 2 x 2048 = 4096 in-flight tokens (default max_num_batched_tokens 2048 for an under-70 GiB GPU on the API server, arg_utils.py:2997-3002). Sliding reservation = cdiv(1023+4096,16)+1 = 321 blocks = 5136 tokens x 327,680 B = 1.567 GiB BF16 / 0.784 GiB FP8 (kv_cache_interface.py:918-955). This is the open regression #49878. Corrected study-method numbers: pool 14.647 - 9.559 - 1.2 = 3.888 GiB. BF16 max = (3.888-1.567) GiB / 16384 = about 152,100 tokens. FP8 = (3.888-0.784)/8192 = about 406,900, capped at 262,144. Tied-lm_head variant (7.685 GiB resident): pool 5.762 GiB, BF16 262,144 needs 4.0+1.567 = 5.567 GiB, so it still fits but with only about 0.2 GiB headroom.

verdicts.claim: --max-model-len 131072 with BF16 KV fits with about 0.95 GiB spare; 262144 with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 fits
verdicts.correction: Both still fit, but the BF16 131072 margin is smaller: it needs 2.0 + 1.567 = 3.567 GiB of a 3.888 GiB pool, leaving about 0.32 GiB, not 0.95. FP8 262144 needs 2.0 + 0.784 = 2.78 GiB. Each extra concurrent sequence costs another 1.57 GiB BF16 / 0.78 GiB FP8 of sliding cache, so with --max-num-seqs 2 a second long request may wait at BF16 131072.

summary:
The record mostly holds. I re-read every file size, the config, the vLLM v0.33.0 registry, parsers, Marlin path and TRITON_ATTN forcing, plus llama.cpp b12418 arch, chat detection and FA D=512 support, and all of it matches.

One load-bearing correction: v0.33.0 enables async scheduling by default, so sliding-window KV is reserved for 2 x 2048 in-flight tokens (5136 tokens = 1.567 GiB BF16, 0.784 GiB FP8), not 3071 tokens (open issue #49878). With the study method, BF16 max context drops from about 193K to about 152K. 131072 BF16 still fits, but with about 0.32 GiB spare instead of 0.95. FP8 still reaches the 262,144 cap.

The safetensors header confirms the duplicate 2.01 GB lm_head, and vLLM ties it. Gap resolved: llama.cpp also stores V separately for K=V layers (V gets a different norm), so there is no halving.

Issues the record missed: vLLM #53658 (TRITON_ATTN illegal access when a capture size exceeds max-model-len, first hit on gemma-4-12B with a 5090) and llama.cpp #29655 (unstable Gemma 4 multi-line streamed tool calls, which matters for OpenCode edit tools). Also, llama.cpp's GitHub 'latest' is v1.0.0 (2026-11-13); bNNNN builds are pre-releases.

Remaining gaps: no measured tok/s or VRAM on an RTX 5080 Laptop, and the in-image template path and Ollama per-tag sizes are unverified. Recommended: W4A16 + FP8 KV at 131072 with max-num-seqs 1.
